title: Educating Foreign Workers on Available Channels to Settle Wage Disputes and Laws against Illegal Assembly
what_it_is: Educating Foreign Workers on Available Channels to Settle Wage Disputes and Laws against Illegal Assembly

sections.label: Migrant worker education on rights
sections.summary: The SIP educates migrant workers in native languages on employment rights, support channels and lawful behaviour, with guides and outreach via MOM and partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Conducted in native languages, the SIP educates MWs comprehensively on their employment rights, support channels, as well as on lawful and responsible behaviour, including the law against unlawful assembly or procession in public places.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM has developed a comprehensive MW guide, monthly newsletters as well as various infographics in native languages on topics, such as salary payment and channels to seek help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM and its partners also routinely disseminate information through online and physical platforms, for example, FWMOMCare application, social media posts, roadshows as well as events, to remind MWs of their employment rights and encourage those with employment issues to seek help from MOM and the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) for salary claims.

sections.label: TADM monthly salary claims
sections.summary: In 2022, TADM handled about 160 salary claims from migrant workers monthly, compared to 410 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: On average, in 2022, TADM handles about 160 salary claims from MWs each month, compared to 410 in 2019, pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Workers with salary claims
sections.summary: Of the 10 workers involved in the incident, five had salary claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Of the 10 workers that were involved in the incident, five of them had salary claims.

sections.label: Main contractor owed salaries
sections.summary: Main contractor Shanghai Chong Kee owed salary payments to 268 migrant workers, and as at 31 October had settled the owed payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In this case, we also investigated their main contractor – because these are subcontractors servicing the main contractor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We found that the main contractor, Shanghai Chong Kee, owed salary payments to 268 MWs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As at 31 October, Shanghai Chong Kee had settled the owed payments and we are working with them on the payment schedule for the rest.

sections.label: Electronic salary payment requirement
sections.summary: Since April 2020, employers are required to pay migrant workers, especially those in dormitories, salary electronically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since April 2020, when we had the circuit breaker and we made the commitment that all workers were going to be paid, we introduced a requirement for all employers to pay salary electronically for their MWs, especially those who are residing in dormitories.
